Rhea (ML Eng): Hey team — thinking about applying for our "dual-homebase nomad" pilot: alternating 8 weeks Lisbon / 8 weeks SF, starting Sep 2026. Questions: 1) How would WFH stipend and equipment reimbursement work for a formalized recurring split? 2) Any payroll/tax residency exposure if I spend ~6 months total in Portugal across the year but never >90 consecutive days? 3) Would the company need to register locally if multiple people do this? 4) Can Facilities help with EU shipments and VAT for a long-term rented monitor?
Jordan (People Ops): Great question and exciting pilot idea. Immediate notes: stipend is prorated by days at declared locations; for a recurring pattern we can set up a split-homebase record so Payroll and Benefits automatically compute proration each month. Please submit the dual-homebase pilot form (link in bio) and include the proposed schedule. We'll treat this as "recurring temporary remote" and document expected months in each country.
Ravi (Payroll): Payroll perspective: Portuguese tax residency generally uses a 183-day or habitual abode test, but there are other tests (center of vital interests). Cumulatively hitting ~6 months across a year but with no single >90-day block is less likely to create automatic residency, but our global tax vendor must review the pattern. Also, Portuguese social security could apply in some cases if local law deems work performed there. Submit the schedule and check the "pilot" box; we'll request a vendor memo.
Marcus (Legal): Legal: company-level permanent establishment risk is driven by sustained local business activities, employees habitually working, and meetings with local customers/partners. If multiple employees adopt this pattern in Lisbon, we may need to register. For a single participant, low but non-zero. Please include whether you'll meet any Lisbon-based partners or host workshops there. If yes, Legal needs to evaluate mitigations.
Saanvi (Benefits): Benefits: health plan coverage continues, but provider networks vary in EU. For regular EU stays we recommend confirming telemedicine + private clinic options in Lisbon. Also note some benefits (dental, physio) might not apply or have limited coverage. If you're taking meds, check mail forwarding rules. We'll run a benefits portability check after the form is in.
Rhea (ML Eng): No local customers planned; primarily internal work and occasional conference attendance. Would like to keep one company monitor in Lisbon to avoid repeated shipping.
Mateo (Facilities): We can provision a monitor as "long-term loan" in EU. Two logistics options: 1) Ship from US with customs paperwork and declared insurance (VAT/duties possible), or 2) Procure locally in EU and mark as company asset (may require local invoice & VAT reclaim process). Option 2 usually faster and cheaper for multi-months. Pick the asset-procurement option on the form and we'll estimate cost + lead time.
Ravi (Payroll): Also note: stipend is payroll income taxed per your withholding. If you want to avoid taxable payroll complications in a host country we can consider reimbursing coworking or housing costs via expense (non-payroll) for the pilot months, but Legal & Tax would need to sign off. We'll provide a simulation once schedule submitted.
tax-bot: Automated: pilot arrangements that create recurring cross-border patterns will be routed to global tax vendor for a consolidated risk memo. Please include yearly schedule and any planned local hires or contractors. (Ref TAX-PILOT-2026)
Rhea (ML Eng): Good to know. If the company procures locally, does that complicate equity/tax reporting for the asset? I want no surprises on personal tax treatment of perks.
Marcus (Legal): Local procurement of equipment typically stays company-owned and shouldn't affect personal tax materially, but some jurisdictions treat employer-provided benefits as taxable in-kind benefits. We'll confirm with tax vendor. Add a note to the pilot form saying "company-owned asset in PT" so Finance can coordinate. 
Saanvi (Benefits): One more: equity vesting continues while active. However, if you change tax residence at any point, exercise events can have different withholding and reporting. Ari (Equity Admin) will be looped if the vendor flags residency changes.
Rhea (ML Eng): Awesome. Timeline: I'll file the dual-homebase pilot form tonight and attach the recurring schedule. Anything else I should include to speed vendor review?
Jordan (People Ops): Include: 1) exact dates for the next 12 months, 2) activity note (internal-only, no local hiring), 3) equipment preference (ship vs procure), and 4) manager sign-off. We'll fast-track reviewers (Payroll/Legal/Benefits/Facilities) and aim for a consolidated response within 5 business days.
payroll-bot: Action: after form submission payroll will queue a simulation and vendor review (PR-Q-247500). Expect an email thread. 
legal-bot: Note: Legal will review once pilot form marked "dual-homebase". If multiple pilots are approved in Lisbon we will convene a nexus review with Finance.
Rhea (ML Eng): Form submitted, schedule attached (8w PT / 8w SF repeating). Chose local procurement option for the monitor. Manager sign-off attached. Thanks folks 
Jordan (People Ops): Received. We'll coordinate internal reviews and reply with simulated payroll + benefit notes within 5 business days. If any risk is identified we'll propose mitigation (expense-only for coworking, restricted client-facing activities in PT, etc.). Thanks for filing this proactively 🙏
Rhea (ML Eng): Thanks, appreciate the quick help! :raised_hands:
